projects.title: Microcontroller based DC motor speed control
projects.description: Designed and implemented a closed-loop feedback-based speed control software algorithm on a PIC Microcontroller for a 2.5 W DC motor. The algorithm utilizes Pulse Width Modulation (<l>PWM</l>) to regulate the DC power supply to the motor. Motor speed is sensed using a photo interrupter sensor setup across the motor's spindle. The microcontroller's PWM module generates the PWM signal according to the implemented algorithm. This signal is then connected to a driver circuit, which controls the power supply to the DC motor. The control software continuously adjusts the width of the PWM switching signal based on the calculated difference between the sensed speed and the user-desired speed. The user-desired speed is set using an adjustable potentiometer.

projects.title: Feature extraction and classification of ECG signals using Discrete Wavelet Transform & Artificial Neural Networks
projects.description: Developed an algorithm in <l>MATLAB<l> for classifying Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. Utilizing MATLAB's built-in functions, an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was implemented for signal analysis. The PhysioNet ECG Database was utilized for training and testing the ANN model. Statistical parameters, such as standard deviation, mean, and variance, were extracted from the wavelet coefficients of the ECG signal, serving as features for abnormality detection.

projects.title: <l>Wireless Embedded System for Powerline Monitoring</l>
projects.description:
Designed and implemented a wireless embedded system, utilizing WiFi and IEEE 802.15.4 technologies, for real-time monitoring of electric parameters in power transmission lines. The system comprised the following sub-modules:
  1. A pair of Hall effect based transducers for sensing the voltage & current.
  2. Microcontroller with built in ADC modules for signal processing.
  3. WiFi & ZigBee based Wireless transceiver modules for wireless communication.
  4. Personal Computer for Visualization.
The software, developed in C# and .NET using Visual Studio, provided real-time visualization of:
  • Time domain representation of voltage & current waveforms.
  • Frequency domain representation of voltage or current signal.
  • Phasor diagram showing phase difference between voltage & current waveforms.
  • RMS values of voltage and current.

projects.title: Simulation of 4-Bit Microprocessor
projects.description:
Simulated a 4-bit microprocessor in ModelSim HDL Simulator using Verilog Hardware Description Language (HDL). This simulation was accompanied by a custom assembly language compiler software, written in C programming language. The system comprised the following sub-modules:
  • Basic Gates in Data Flow modeling
  • Ripple Carry Adder using Structural modeling
  • Arithmetic & Logic Unit (ALU) using Structural modeling
  • Decoder using Behavioral modelling
  • RAM (Random Access Memory) & Buffers using Dataflow modeling
  • Finite State Machine using Behavioral modeling
  • All Sub-Modules Integrated using Structural modeling
  • Assembly language compiler written in C programming language.

projects.title: Wireless Di-Wheel Robot for Navigation on Predefined Routes
projects.description: Designed and implemented a computer-controlled di-wheeled robot using a PIC16F877 microcontroller, a 27 MHz wireless RC kit, and a pair of geared DC motors, each with a 2 Watts power rating. Routes consisting of straight lines with 45° or 90° bends were created using Microsoft Paint software and stored as bitmap images. The bitmap images were processed using a custom image processing algorithm written and implemented in MATLAB. This algorithm converted the images into ASCII-formatted byte sequences containing information about distances and bend angles. The byte sequences were transmitted to the microcontroller via the PC's <l>RS232</l> serial interface. An assembly language algorithm running on the microcontroller decoded the received byte stream and controlled the voltage levels at the control button pins of the RC kit's remote transmitter. The wireless receiver module received the signals sent by the remote transmitter and decoded them. The onboard driver circuit then drove the motors attached to the robot's wheels according to the decoded byte codes. The robot moved in straight lines for specific distances, turned at precise angles, and repeated these steps until the signal transmission was completed, which occurred when the byte stream transmission corresponding to the route was finished.
